title: Operational knobs (scheduler concurrency, job retention defaults, update repo, MRU size) are config-file-only — no Settings UI
existing_state: Several live, consumed settings exist only as JSON fields with no editor anywhere in the UI: MaxConcurrentJobs (Models/AppConfiguration.cs:140, consumed by JobExecutionService.cs:140), DefaultMaxHistoryRuns / DefaultHistoryRetentionDays / MaxJobOutputCharsPerHost (AppConfiguration.cs:146-158, consumed by SchedulerHistoryPolicyResolver.cs:17-19), MaxRecentFiles (AppConfiguration.cs:128, enforced at Form1.cs:9113), and GitHubOwner/GitHubRepo for the update source (AppConfiguration.cs:447-452, used at Form1.cs:375-376). A grep of SettingsDialog.cs finds none of them. Changing scheduler parallelism — a knob a 200-device operator genuinely needs — requires hand-editing config.json while the app is closed, in the same single file that holds all presets and environments (one typo triggers the corrupt-config path).
recommendation: Add a small 'Scheduler' group to SettingsDialog (concurrent jobs, default max runs per job, default retention days, max output per host) and an 'Advanced' group (recent-files count; update owner/repo behind an 'advanced' expander since forks/private mirrors are the use case). All are simple NumericUpDown/TextBox bindings into the existing config Update() flow — the persistence plumbing already exists.
user_benefit: Power users get safe, discoverable control over scheduler throughput and retention instead of risky hand-edits of the app's single most valuable file; most users will discover these capabilities exist at all.

evidence.note: grep for all listed knobs returns no matches in the dialog
